claim: The first 350 amino acids of AKAP79 contain extended regions of intrinsic disorder.
source: Analysis with IUPred (Dosztányi et al., 2005) and PONDR (Li et al., 1999) predict extended regions of disorder within the first 350 amino acids of AKAP79, whereas the C-terminal portion of the anchoring protein is more ordered (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatic predictions using IUPred and PONDR algorithms, and shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The C-terminal region of AKAP79 is more ordered than the N-terminal region.
source: Analysis with IUPred (Dosztányi et al., 2005) and PONDR (Li et al., 1999) predict extended regions of disorder within the first 350 amino acids of AKAP79, whereas the C-terminal portion of the anchoring protein is more ordered (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by bioinformatic predictions using IUPred and PONDR algorithms, and shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The C-terminal region of AKAP79 encompasses the PKA-binding helix.
source: This is consistent with evidence showing that the C-terminal region encompasses the PKA-binding helix (blue; Carr et al., 1991; Gold et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies by Carr et al., 1991 and Gold et al., 2006.

claim: AKAP79 contains known binding sites for protein kinase C/calmodulin.
source: These include known binding sites within AKAP79 for protein kinase C/calmodulin (green) and PP2B (red) (Coghlan et al., 1995; Dell'Acqua et al., 2002; Faux and Scott, 1997; Klauck et al., 1996; Oliveria et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: AKAP79 contains known binding sites for PP2B.
source: These include known binding sites within AKAP79 for protein kinase C/calmodulin (green) and PP2B (red) (Coghlan et al., 1995; Dell'Acqua et al., 2002; Faux and Scott, 1997; Klauck et al., 1996; Oliveria et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: AKAP79 contains a short linear motif at residues 122-136 of unknown function.
source: Short linear motifs of unknown function were also evident, including a prominent peak at residues 122–136 of the anchoring protein (Figure 1C and D, orange).
evidence: Identified by ANCHOR and SLiMPred predictions shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: The AKAP79-PP2B-CaM sub-complex has a molecular mass of 160 kDa as determined by SEC-MALS.
source: However, quantitative analysis with in-line multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS) revealed a monodispersed complex of 160 kDa (Figure 1J).
evidence: Measured by SEC-MALS analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The AKAP79-PP2B-CaM sub-complex contains a 1:1:1:1 ratio of protein components.
source: This corresponds to a 1:1:1:1 ratio of protein components within the AKAP79-PP2B-CaM sub-complex.
evidence: Inferred from the 160 kDa molecular mass determined by SEC-MALS.

claim: AKAP79 complexes are intrinsically disordered.
source: Since intrinsically disordered proteins often elute from size-exclusion columns early, we suggest that AKAP79 complexes are disordered.
evidence: Inferred from the early elution behavior in size-exclusion chromatography.

claim: Dormant AKAP79-PP2B holoenzyme complexes exist in a variety of flexible and extended topologies.
source: Thus, dormant AKAP79-PP2B holoenzyme complexes exist in a variety of flexible and extended topologies.
evidence: Supported by EM analysis showing particles varying in length from 160 to 240 Å.

claim: Dormant AKAP79-PP2B complexes vary in particle length from 160 to 240 Å.
source: These models, although of similar width and depth (Figure 3C–E, bottom) vary in length from 160 to 240 Å (Figure 3C–E, top).
evidence: Measured from 3D EM models shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: Dormant AKAP79-PP2B complexes segregate into two populations with mean lengths of 184 ± 16 Å and 228 ± 5 Å.
source: Particles segregated into two populations with mean lengths of 184 ± 16 Å (n = 7499) and 228 ± 5 Å (n = 3153, Figure 3B, blue).
evidence: Measured from histogram analysis of class averages shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complexes are more uniform than dormant complexes.
source: In contrast, active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complexes are more uniform.
evidence: Supported by EM analysis showing a single population of particles.

claim: Active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complexes have a mean length of 178 ± 17 Å.
source: Reference-based alignment of a refined data set of 20,461 elements yielded 25 representative classes that segregated into a single population of active particles with a mean length of 178 ± 17 Å (Figure 3F and G, orange).
evidence: Measured from histogram analysis shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: Active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complexes are more compact and globular than dormant complexes.
source: Three-dimensional rendering of representative AKAP79/PP2B/CaM classes reveals more compact and globular complexes (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: Shown by 3D EM models in Figure 3H-J.

claim: Both dormant and active AKAP79-PP2B macromolecular units occupy similar volumes of 7.4 × 10^5 Å^3.
source: Yet both the dormant and the active macromolecular units occupy similar volumes (7.4 × 105 Å3), when isosurface thresholds are set to match 2-D averages.
evidence: Measured from EM models with matched isosurface thresholds.

claim: Additional intermolecular contacts within the active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complex sustain a more globular topology.
source: This implies that additional intermolecular contacts residing within the active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complex sustain a more globular topology.
evidence: Inferred from the similar volumes but different topologies of dormant and active complexes.

claim: The N-terminus of AKAP79 localizes to a density at the top of the active complex.
source: First, Fab fragments of IgG against the MBP tag localized the N-terminus of AKAP79 in a density at the top of a predominant class average (Figure 4A–G).
evidence: Determined by Fab labeling experiments shown in Figure 4A-G.

claim: The C-terminus of AKAP79 localizes to the core of the active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complex.
source: Second, a 1.8 nm nanogold-NiNTA conjugate labeled the His-tag on the C-terminus of the anchoring protein (Figure 4H–M). Gold particles decorated the core of the active AKAP79/PP2B/CaM complex (Figure 4J and M).
evidence: Determined by nanogold labeling experiments shown in Figure 4H-M.

claim: The catalytic A subunit of PP2B localizes to the lower lobe of the active macromolecular assembly.
source: Third, Fab fragments against Flag-tagged A subunit of PP2B localized the catalytic subunit of the phosphatase in the lower lobe of the macromolecular assembly (Figure 4N–R).
evidence: Determined by Fab labeling experiments shown in Figure 4N-R.

claim: In the dormant complex, residues 337-343 of AKAP79 (PIAIIIT motif) is the only site of contact with PP2B.
source: In the dormant complex, a consensus PP2B interaction motif located between residues 337–343 of AKAP79 (PIAIIIT) was the only site of contact with the phosphatase (Figure 5A red and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Determined by chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5A and Supplementary file 1.

claim: In the active complex, four additional AKAP79-PP2B A subunit interfaces are evident beyond the PIAIIIT motif.
source: In contrast, a total of four additional AKAP79-PP2B A subunit interfaces were evident in the active complex (Figure 5B, red).
evidence: Determined by chemical cross-linking and mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The additional AKAP-interactive peptides in the active complex reside within the lower lobe of the catalytic subunit of PP2B.
source: These ancillary AKAP-interactive peptides reside within the lower lobe of the catalytic subunit of PP2B (Figure 5C and D, green, blue, teal and lime) and are proximal to a previously defined binding surface for the PIAIIIT motif (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: Shown by mapping cross-linked peptides onto PP2B structure in Figure 5C and D, with citation to Li et al., 2012.

claim: A cross-link between lysine 126 on AKAP79 and lysine 165 on the B subunit of PP2B was exclusively detected in the active complex.
source: ReACT also identified a cross-link between lysine 126 on AKAP79 and lysine 165 on the B subunit of PP2B (Figure 5B, orange). This peptide pair was exclusively detected in the active complex.
evidence: Determined by ReACT analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Amino terminal regions of AKAP79 contact the B subunit of the active phosphatase holoenzyme.
source: We can therefore infer that amino terminal regions of the anchoring protein contact the B subunit of the active phosphatase holoenzyme (Figure 5C and D, orange peptide).
evidence: Inferred from cross-linking data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: The AKAP79 sequence Leu-Lys-Ile-Pro resembles a consensus LxVP phosphatase interaction module.
source: A recognizable feature of the AKAP79 peptide is the sequence Leu-Lys-Ile-Pro, which resembles a consensus LxVP phosphatase interaction module (Rodríguez et al., 2009; Sheftic et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Rodríguez et al., 2009 and Sheftic et al., 2016.

claim: The LKIP sequence is located within a disordered region of AKAP79 predicted to form a short linear interaction motif.
source: Interestingly, this sequence is located within a disordered region of the anchoring protein predicted to form a short linear interaction motif (Figure 1D and E, orange bar).
evidence: Shown by bioinformatic predictions in Figure 1D and E.

claim: Molecular modeling predicts that the core LKIP motif on AKAP79 slots into the drug-binding pocket on PP2B.
source: Molecular modeling predicts that the core Leu-Lys-Ile-Pro (LKIP) motif on AKAP79 slots into this drug-binding pocket on PP2B (Figure 5G).
evidence: Predicted by molecular modeling shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Residues downstream of the LKIP motif contact PP2B.
source: Yet, one distinction is that residues downstream of this motif contact PP2B (Figure 5G).
evidence: Shown by molecular modeling in Figure 5G.

claim: Conventional PP2B interacting partners utilize determinants upstream of the LxVP motif to enhance binding affinity.
source: This is in contrast to conventional PP2B interacting partners that utilize determinants upstream of the LxVP motif to enhance the binding affinity for targeting subunits (Sheftic et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sheftic et al., 2016.

claim: Residues 122 to 136 of AKAP79 form a Ca2+-responsive PP2B-binding region.
source: Residues 122 to 136 of AKAP79 formed a Ca2+ responsive PP2B-binding region (Figure 6B).
evidence: Determined by solid-phase spot-array analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Determinants flanking the core LKIP quadrapeptide contribute to Ca2+-dependent phosphatase anchoring.
source: Notably, determinants flanking the core Leu-Lys-Ile-Pro quadrapeptide (residues 125–128; LKIP) contributed to Ca2+-dependent phosphatase anchoring, since pretreatment with EDTA abolished all protein-protein interactions (Figure 6B).
evidence: Determined by spot-array analysis with EDTA treatment shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 binds to PP2B only in the presence of Ca2+/CaM.
source: Immunoblot analysis demonstrated that the N-terminal fragment bound to the phosphatase only in the presence of Ca2+/CaM (Figure 6D, top panel, lane 2).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 6D.

claim: N-terminal AKAP79-PP2B binding is lost upon chelation of calcium.
source: Binding was also lost upon chelation of calcium (Figure 6D, top panel, lane 3).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down assays with EDTA shown in Figure 6D.

claim: PP2B binding is abolished when the LKIP motif is deleted from the N-terminal fragment of AKAP79.
source: Likewise, PP2B binding was abolished when experiments were repeated with a mutant N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 that lacked the LKIP motif (Figure 6D, top panel lanes 5–8).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down assays with deletion mutant shown in Figure 6D.

claim: AKAP79-associated PP2B retains full activity.
source: In parallel, phosphatase activity measurements using the small molecule substrate (diFMUP) demonstrated that AKAP79 associated-PP2B retained full activity (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Measured by phosphatase activity assays shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 encompassing the LKIP motif binds PP2B with a Kd of 81 μM.
source: An N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 encompassing the LKIP motif bound PP2B with a Kd of 81 μM (n = 4) as compared to binding affinities of 5.6 μM and 12 μM for the PIAIIIT region and the full-length AKAP respectively (both n = 4; Figure 6E).
evidence: Measured by AlphaScreen competition assays shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The PIAIIIT region of AKAP79 binds PP2B with a Kd of 5.6 μM.
source: An N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 encompassing the LKIP motif bound PP2B with a Kd of 81 μM (n = 4) as compared to binding affinities of 5.6 μM and 12 μM for the PIAIIIT region and the full-length AKAP respectively (both n = 4; Figure 6E).
evidence: Measured by AlphaScreen competition assays shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Full-length AKAP79 binds PP2B with a Kd of 12 μM.
source: An N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 encompassing the LKIP motif bound PP2B with a Kd of 81 μM (n = 4) as compared to binding affinities of 5.6 μM and 12 μM for the PIAIIIT region and the full-length AKAP respectively (both n = 4; Figure 6E).
evidence: Measured by AlphaScreen competition assays shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The PIAIIIT motif is the primary determinant for PP2B anchoring.
source: These measurements further indicate that the PIAIIIT motif is the primary determinant for PP2B anchoring, whereas the LKIP region provides an auxiliary interaction.
evidence: Inferred from the binding affinity measurements showing PIAIIIT has higher affinity than LKIP.

claim: The LKIP region provides an auxiliary interaction for PP2B anchoring.
source: These measurements further indicate that the PIAIIIT motif is the primary determinant for PP2B anchoring, whereas the LKIP region provides an auxiliary interaction.
evidence: Inferred from the binding affinity measurements showing LKIP has lower affinity than PIAIIIT but still contributes to binding.

claim: Two aromatic amino acids (W352 and F356) on PP2B form a binding pocket for LxVP motifs.
source: Mechanistic and crystallographic analysis of PP2B has identified two aromatic amino acids (W352 and F356) that form a binding pocket for LxVP motifs (Figure 6F) (Rodríguez et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rodríguez et al., 2009 and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The W352A/F356A mutant of PP2B has reduced binding to the N-terminal fragment of AKAP79.
source: When both residues were substituted with alanine (W352A/F356A), we noted that this mutant had reduced binding to the N-terminal fragment of AKAP79 in GST pulldown assays (Figure 6G, top panel; lane 6).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 6G.

claim: AKAP79 fragments encompassing the PIAIIIT motif retain the ability to bind wildtype and W352A/F356A mutant PP2B.
source: Control experiments confirmed that the AKAP79 fragments encompassing the PIAIIIT motif retained the ability to bind wildtype and mutant PP2B (Figure 6G top panel, lanes 7 and 8).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down assays shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The LKIP region on AKAP79 utilizes a similar mode of interaction analogous to LxVP motifs.
source: Together, these results indicate that the LKIP region on AKAP79 utilizes a similar mode of interaction analogous, but not identical to LxVP motifs.
evidence: Inferred from the mutational analysis and structural comparisons.

claim: Residues immediately upstream of the LxVP core motif contribute to PP2B-selective binding.
source: A recent study has suggested that residues immediately upstream of the LxVP core motif (−1 and −2 positions) contribute to PP2B-selective binding (Sheftic et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sheftic et al., 2016.

claim: AKAP79 utilizes distal PP2B binding determinants both upstream and downstream of the LKIP motif.
source: One clear distinction in the AKAP79/PP2B interface is that the anchoring protein utilizes distal PP2B binding determinants both upstream and downstream of the LKIP motif.
evidence: Inferred from the spot-array and cross-linking data showing contacts beyond the core LKIP sequence.

claim: PP2B co-precipitates only with AKAP79-CaNAR and AKAP79∆L-CaNAR constructs.
source: These latter studies detected co-fractionation of PP2B only with AKAP79-CaNAR and AKAP79∆L-CaNAR (Figure 7C, top panel, quantification in Figure 7D).
evidence: Determined by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 7C and quantified in Figure 7D.

claim: Treatment with 1 μM ionomycin augments detection of PP2B in AKAP79 immune complexes.
source: Treatment with 1 μM ionomycin, which increases calcium permeability, augmented detection of PP2B (Figure 7C, top panel, lanes 7 and 8).
evidence: Determined by co-immunoprecipitation experiments with ionomycin treatment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Engaging the LKIP motif favors a stable interaction with AKAP79.
source: Thus, engaging the LKIP motif favors a stable interaction with AKAP79.
evidence: Inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data showing enhanced PP2B binding with ionomycin treatment.

claim: The AKAP79∆L-CaNAR variant reaches half maximal response in 2.41 ± 0.24 min.
source: The AKAP79∆L-CaNAR variant reached half maximal response in 2.41 ± 0.24 min as compared to 3.58 ± 0.20 min for the full-length reporter (Figure 7G).
evidence: Measured from FRET imaging experiments shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The full-length AKAP79-CaNAR reporter reaches half maximal response in 3.58 ± 0.20 min.
source: The AKAP79∆L-CaNAR variant reached half maximal response in 2.41 ± 0.24 min as compared to 3.58 ± 0.20 min for the full-length reporter (Figure 7G).
evidence: Measured from FRET imaging experiments shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The change in kinetics of AKAP79∆L-CaNAR does not depend on the expression level of the CaNAR reporter.
source: This change in kinetics did not depend on the expression level of the CaNAR reporter as determined by linear regression analysis of the data (R-squared values of less than 0.1, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Determined by linear regression analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The AKAP79∆L-CaNAR reporter exhibits statistically higher maximal FRET responses than the native reporter at 100 nM ionomycin.
source: Accordingly, when experiments were repeated with a ten-fold lower concentration of ionomycin (100 nM), the AKAP79∆L-CaNAR reporter exhibited statistically higher maximal FRET responses than the native reporter (Figure 7H–J).
evidence: Measured from FRET imaging experiments at 100 nM ionomycin shown in Figure 7H-J.

claim: Total calcium responses are equivalent in the presence of both AKAP79-CaNAR and AKAP79∆L-CaNAR reporters.
source: Control imaging with the genetically encoded calcium indicator RCaMP confirmed that total calcium responses were equivalent in the presence of both modified CaNAR reporters (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Measured by RCaMP calcium imaging shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The LKIP motif serves to desensitize PP2B towards low levels of calcium.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that the LKIP motif serves to desensitize PP2B towards low levels of calcium, while still allowing the anchored phosphatase to maintain maximal activity when calcium concentrations are elevated.
evidence: Inferred from the FRET imaging experiments showing differential responses at low and high calcium levels.

claim: The LKIP motif allows anchored PP2B to maintain maximal activity when calcium concentrations are elevated.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that the LKIP motif serves to desensitize PP2B towards low levels of calcium, while still allowing the anchored phosphatase to maintain maximal activity when calcium concentrations are elevated.
evidence: Inferred from the FRET imaging experiments showing similar maximal responses at high calcium levels.

claim: Engagement of the LKIP motif on AKAP79 stabilizes a conformation of PP2B that does not relieve auto-inhibition as readily as non-anchored phosphatase.
source: Rather, it is likely that upon Ca2+/CaM influx, engagement of the LKIP motif on AKAP79 stabilizes a conformation of PP2B that does not relieve auto-inhibition as readily as non-anchored phosphatase.
evidence: Inferred from the FRET imaging data showing altered kinetics with the LKIP motif.

claim: The LKIP motif in AKAP79 serves to fine-tune the calcium sensitivity of anchored and active PP2B.
source: Thus, we propose that the LKIP motif in AKAP79 serves to fine-tune the calcium sensitivity of anchored and active PP2B.
evidence: Proposed based on the FRET imaging data showing differential calcium sensitivity.

claim: Cyclosporin A/cyclophilin A cocktails diminish binding of PP2B to the N-terminal region of AKAP79.
source: Competition experiments performed with cyclosporin A/cyclophilin A cocktails (2 μM) diminished binding of PP2B to the N-terminal region of AKAP79 as assessed by western blot (Figure 8A–B; top panel, lane 4).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down competition assays shown in Figure 8A-B.

claim: The immunosuppressant drug cyclosporin has no effect on PP2B binding to AKAP79 fragments encompassing the PIAIIIT sequence.
source: In contrast, the immunosuppressant drug had no effect on PP2B binding to AKAP79 fragments encompassing the PIAIIIT sequence (Figure 8A–B, top panel, lanes 5–8).
evidence: Determined by GST pull-down competition assays shown in Figure 8A-B.

claim: The LKIP motif and flanking determinants on AKAP79 may influence the clinical action of immunosuppressant drugs.
source: Importantly, these results indicate that the LKIP motif and flanking determinants on AKAP79 not only modulate calcium responsive PP2B anchoring, but also may influence the clinical action of immunosuppressant drugs.
evidence: Inferred from the cyclosporin competition experiments.

claim: Conformational flexibility within AKAP79-PP2B complexes is a fundamental element of their molecular action.
source: Using a combined negative-stain EM and chemical cross-linking strategy we discover that conformational flexibility within AKAP79-PP2B complexes is a fundamental element of their molecular action.
evidence: Concluded from the EM and cross-linking studies presented in the manuscript.

claim: Intrinsic disorder within ancillary targeting components confers a dynamic range of enzyme action for anchored signaling enzymes.
source: A key facet of this emerging concept is that anchored signaling enzymes are not only tethered to subcellular organelles, but intrinsic disorder within ancillary targeting components confers a dynamic range of enzyme action.
evidence: Proposed based on the structural findings and broader context of anchored enzyme function.

claim: Flexible linker regions within each regulatory subunit (RII) of anchored PKA confer a ~200 Å radius of motion to the associated catalytic subunits.
source: For example, flexible linker regions within each regulatory subunit (RII) of anchored Protein Kinase A (PKA) confer a ∼200 Å radius of motion to the associated catalytic subunits (Smith et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Smith et al., 2013.

claim: Anchored PKA holoenzymes remain intact, active and proximal to substrates within signaling islands.
source: More recently we have shown that these anchored PKA holoenzymes remain intact, active and proximal to substrates within these newly defined signaling islands (Smith et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Smith et al., 2017.

claim: Association with AKAPs exerts allosteric effects that protect PKC isoforms from ATP-competitive inhibitors.
source: In other cellular contexts, association with AKAPs exerts allosteric effects that protect PKC isoforms from ATP-competitive inhibitors (Hoshi et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hoshi et al., 2010.

claim: Protein-protein interactions contribute to the substrate preference of promiscuous enzymes.
source: These observations indicate that protein-protein interactions contribute to the substrate preference of these often-promiscuous enzymes, and in a broader context point towards intrinsic disorder and conformational flexibility as inherent specificity determinants of anchored enzyme scaffolds.
evidence: Inferred from the examples of PKA and PKC regulation by AKAPs.

claim: Intrinsic disorder and conformational flexibility are inherent specificity determinants of anchored enzyme scaffolds.
source: These observations indicate that protein-protein interactions contribute to the substrate preference of these often-promiscuous enzymes, and in a broader context point towards intrinsic disorder and conformational flexibility as inherent specificity determinants of anchored enzyme scaffolds.
evidence: Proposed based on the findings in this study and cited examples.

claim: Phosphatase activation induces a topological reorganization of AKAP79-PP2B assemblies.
source: Another new concept uncovered by our EM analyses is that phosphatase activation induces a topological reorganization of AKAP79-PP2B assemblies.
evidence: Concluded from the EM analysis showing different conformations in dormant vs. active states.

claim: Upon addition of Ca2+/calmodulin, dormant AKAP79-PP2B assemblies transition from extended multi-lobal conformations into more globular structures.
source: We base this conclusion on single-particle EM evidence in Figure 3 showing that upon addition of Ca2+/calmodulin, dormant AKAP79-PP2B assemblies transition from an assortment of extended multi-lobal conformations into more globular structures.
evidence: Shown by EM analysis in Figure 3.

claim: The PIAIIIT motif at residues 337-343 of AKAP79 is a stable PP2B-anchoring determinant that forms the conformational core for dormant assemblies.
source: The crosslinking studies in Figure 5 implicate the PIAIIIT motif at residues 337–343 of AKAP79 as a stable PP2B-anchoring determinant that forms the conformational core for dormant assemblies.
evidence: Determined by cross-linking studies shown in Figure 5.

claim: The bi-modal distribution in dormant particle sizes may reflect the differential deployment of SLiMs that act synergistically with the PIAIIIT anchoring motif.
source: However, the bi-modal distribution in particle sizes highlighted in Figure 3C may reflect the differential deployment of other SLiMs that act synergistically with the PIAIIIT anchoring motif (Grigoriu et al., 2013; Rodríguez et al., 2009; Roy et al., 2007).
evidence: Speculated based on the bi-modal distribution observed in Figure 3C, with citations to related studies.

claim: Additional SLiMs are engaged within the active assembly to drive the formation of a more compact, but fully active phosphatase-anchoring protein unit.
source: This configuration is radically altered upon activation with Ca2+/CaM as the aforementioned topological variants consolidate into a single population with a mean particle length of 178 Å. Hence, additional SLiMs are engaged within the active assembly to drive the formation of a more compact, but fully active phosphatase-anchoring protein unit.
evidence: Inferred from the EM and cross-linking data showing conformational changes upon activation.

claim: The LxVP motif was originally identified as a rudimentary PP2B substrate recognition site that enhances dephosphorylation of the RII subunit of PKA.
source: The LxVP motif was originally identified as a rudimentary PP2B substrate recognition site that enhances dephosphorylation of the RII subunit of PKA (Blumenthal et al., 1986).
evidence: Supported by citation to Blumenthal et al., 1986.

claim: LxVP motifs augment PP2B binding and dephosphorylation of the NFAT transcription factors.
source: Subsequently, LxVP motifs were shown to augment PP2B binding and dephosphorylation of the NFAT transcription factors (Grigoriu et al., 2013; Rodríguez et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Grigoriu et al., 2013 and Rodríguez et al., 2009.

claim: In KSR2, an LxVP motif is utilized in conjunction with intrinsic disorder to ensure efficient dephosphorylation of serine and threonine residues at sites distal to the PP2B binding site.
source: More recently, a variation on this theme was reported in the MAP kinase scaffolding protein KSR2 where an LxVP motif is utilized in conjunction with intrinsic disorder to ensure efficient dephosphorylation of serine and threonine residues at sites distal to the PP2B binding site (Brennan et al., 2011; Dougherty et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Brennan et al., 2011 and Dougherty et al., 2009.

claim: Flexibility surrounding the PP2B-binding regions of AKAP79 may provide a means to extend the range of anchored phosphatase action.
source: A parallel situation may arise in AKAP79 macromolecular assemblies, as flexibility surrounding the PP2B-binding regions of the anchoring protein may provide a means to extend the range of anchored phosphatase action.
evidence: Speculated based on the analogy to KSR2 and the structural findings.

claim: The LKIP motif on AKAP79 is analogous to the MyPhonE or SILK motifs in PP1-targeting subunits.
source: Scrutiny of type I phosphatase (PP1)-targeting subunit co-crystal structures shows that the LKIP motif on AKAP79 is analogous to the MyPhonE or SILK motifs (Hendrickx et al., 2009).
evidence: Inferred from structural comparison, with citation to Hendrickx et al., 2009.

claim: MyPhonE or SILK motifs act in concert with RVxF targeting elements to manage the PP1 catalytic subunit in various subcellular compartments.
source: These secondary binding determinants act in concert with RVxF targeting elements to manage the PP1 catalytic subunit in a variety of subcellular compartments (Egloff et al., 1997; Roy and Cyert, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Egloff et al., 1997 and Roy and Cyert, 2009.

claim: A protein-protein interaction through LKIP sets distance parameters for anchored phosphatase activity that are contingent on prior association of PP2B A subunit with the PIAIIIT motif.
source: Live cell imaging with AKAP79-CaNAR FRET reporters (Figure 7D and E) expand this concept by showing that a protein-protein interaction through LKIP sets distance parameters for anchored phosphatase activity that are contingent on the prior association of the PP2B A subunit with the PIAIIIT motif.
evidence: Inferred from the FRET imaging data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: The cooperative action of multiple enzyme-binding surfaces, along with the malleability of AKAP, creates an elastic and adaptive signaling environment that permits the phosphatase to reach nearby substrates.
source: Hence, the cooperative action of multiple enzyme-binding surfaces, along with the malleability of the AKAP, creates an elastic and adaptive signaling environment that permits the phosphatase to reach nearby substrates.
evidence: Proposed based on the structural and functional data.

claim: Tissue-specific ablation of PP2B from β-cells generates a diabetic state that includes defects in NFAT transcriptional signaling, diminished insulin biosynthesis and a loss of islet mass.
source: For example, tissue-specific ablation of PP2B from β-cells generates a diabetic state that includes defects in NFAT transcriptional signaling, diminished insulin biosynthesis and a loss of islet mass (Bernal-Mizrachi et al., 2004; Heit et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bernal-Mizrachi et al., 2004 and Heit et al., 2006.

claim: Organ transplant patients who continually receive PP2B inhibitor drugs cyclosporin and FK506 often experience increased blood glucose levels and hypertension as hallmarks of new-onset diabetes after transplant.
source: Likewise, organ transplant patients who continually receive the PP2B inhibitor drugs cyclosporin and FK506 as immunosuppressives often experience increased blood glucose levels and hypertension as hallmarks of a clinical syndrome known as new-onset diabetes after transplant (Heisel et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Heisel et al., 2004.

claim: AKAP150 knockin mice that lack the PIAIIIT motif and incorrectly target the active phosphatase display improved glucose handling and heightened insulin sensitivity.
source: AKAP150 knockin mice that lack the PIAIIIT motif and incorrectly target the active phosphatase display improved glucose handling and heightened insulin sensitivity (Hinke et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hinke et al., 2012.

claim: Mislocalization of PP2B is the predominant molecular event underlying advantageous metabolic phenotypes that counteract symptoms of type II diabetes.
source: This argues that mislocalization of PP2B is the predominant molecular event underlying these advantageous, albeit tissue-specific, metabolic phenotypes that counteract the symptoms of type II diabetes.
evidence: Inferred from the AKAP150 knockin mouse data.

claim: Small molecules or peptidomimetics that perturb PP2B tethering, but do not affect catalytic activity, may boost insulin sensitivity.
source: Thus, small molecules or peptidomimetics that perturb PP2B tethering, but do not affect the catalytic activity, may boost insulin sensitivity (Matsoukas et al., 2015).
evidence: Speculated based on the metabolic phenotypes, with citation to Matsoukas et al., 2015.

claim: Cell-permeable PxIxIT and LxVP peptides can achieve immunosuppression with fewer side effects in animal studies.
source: This theory is further consolidated by animal studies that deliver cell-permeable PxIxIT and LxVP peptides to achieve immunosuppression with fewer side effects (Elloumi et al., 2012; Escolano et al., 2014; Noguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Elloumi et al., 2012, Escolano et al., 2014, and Noguchi et al., 2004.

claim: Engagement of the LKIP sequence attenuates anchored phosphatase activity at low levels of calcium.
source: Live-cell imaging experiments in Figure 7 show that engagement of the LKIP sequence attenuates anchored phosphatase activity at low levels of calcium.
evidence: Shown by FRET imaging experiments in Figure 7.

claim: The attenuation of anchored phosphatase activity by LKIP is relieved upon increased calcium influx.
source: Importantly, these effects are relieved upon increased calcium influx.
evidence: Shown by FRET imaging experiments at different calcium levels.

claim: Proximity or direct association with L-type calcium channels may profoundly influence the temporal action of the anchored phosphatase.
source: Thus, proximity or direct association with L-type calcium channels, as reported by others, may profoundly influence the temporal action of the anchored phosphatase.
evidence: Speculated based on the calcium sensitivity findings and context of L-type calcium channels.

claim: Transient calcium fluctuation is pronounced within the vicinity of L-type calcium channel-AKAP79/150 clusters in the cardiovascular system.
source: This is particularly relevant in the cardiovascular system, where transient calcium fluctuation is pronounced within the vicinity of L-type calcium channel-AKAP79/150 clusters (Nieves-Cintrón et al., 2016; Nystoriak et al., 2014; Nystoriak et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nieves-Cintrón et al., 2016, Nystoriak et al., 2014, and Nystoriak et al., 2017.

claim: AKAP79/150 associated pools of PKA, PKC and PP2B reversibly control neuronal NMDA receptors, L-type calcium channels in the postsynaptic density, and GABA receptors in inhibitory synapses.
source: A similar situation may arise in the brain where neuronal NMDA receptors, L-type calcium channels in the postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses and GABA receptors embedded within inhibitory synapses are reversibly controlled by AKAP79/150 associated pools of PKA, PKC and PP2B (Brandon et al., 2003; Colledge et al., 2000; Jurado et al., 2010; Li et al., 2012; Oliveria et al., 2007; Sanderson et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: LKIP motifs on AKAP79/150 differentially regulate PP2B responses to calcium stimulation and balance the role of CaMKII phosphorylation at synapses.
source: With this in mind, we postulate LKIP motifs on AKAP79/150 differentially regulate PP2B responses to calcium stimulation and hence balance the role of CaMKII phosphorylation at synapses (Derkach et al., 1999; Mulkey et al., 1994).
evidence: Postulated based on the findings, with citations to Derkach et al., 1999 and Mulkey et al., 1994.

claim: Flexibility is a defining feature of AKAP79 complexes.
source: Our discovery that flexibility is a defining feature of AKAP79 complexes points toward a mechanism whereby combinatorial recruitment of binding partners tailors the overall conformation of the macromolecular assembly.
evidence: Concluded from the EM and structural studies.

claim: Combinatorial recruitment of binding partners tailors the overall conformation of AKAP79 macromolecular assemblies.
source: Our discovery that flexibility is a defining feature of AKAP79 complexes points toward a mechanism whereby combinatorial recruitment of binding partners tailors the overall conformation of the macromolecular assembly.
evidence: Proposed based on the structural findings.

claim: Structural versatility represents a new means to shape AKAP79/150 kinase-phosphatase assemblies for their customized physiological roles.
source: Such structural versatility represents a new means to shape AKAP79/150 kinase-phosphatase assemblies for their customized physiological roles.
evidence: Proposed based on the overall findings of the study.
